newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PAKISTAN, INDIA COTTON RATES SEEN RISING NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: PAKISTAN, INDIA COTTON RATES SEEN RISING NEXT WEEK.

text.p: Cotton rates are likely to rise in the next week in Pakistan and India following rains that disrupted supplies from farms to ginneries and markets, dealers in the two countries said on Friday.

In Pakistan, rates rose after factories stopped ginning owing to rains in Sindh province where the 1997/98 (July-June) crop began reaching them earlier than in the main-growing Punjab province, dealer Adil Nasim said.
The private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) on Friday fixed the rate for the 1997/98 crop's NIAB-78 variety 16.88 rupees higher at 2,576.88 rupees per maund (37.32), he said.
Pakistan has set a target of 10 million 375-lb bales for the 1997/98 crop, up from 8.783 million bales in 1996/97 crop, which was hit by pests and untimely rains.
Output had reached 8.783 million bales by June 30, down from 9.938 million at the same time a year ago.
1996/97 crop cotton remained unchanged despite buying by Brazil, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Portugal, Japan, Vietnam and Hong Kong, Nasim said.
Some 19,755 bales were registered for export in the 10 days to July 28, raising export contracts to 190,080 bales by July 28, the KCA said.
The contracts were signed between $0.65 and $0.73 per lb FOB and $0.71 C&F for various destinations, it said.
Pakistan shipped 142,212 bales of cotton by July 19 compared to 1.82 million a year ago, the KCA said.

In the kerb market, new-crop NIAB-78 was quoted at 2,580/2,590 rupees per maund.
In India, cotton prices rose on a limited supply despite poor buying from mills in the week to Thursday, dealers said.
"But speculative buying has triggered a rise in prices as traders reported a shortage of ready stock," said Mahesh Thakkar, a leading Indian cotton dealer.
He said most mills had enough stocks to last up to three months and see them through the current season ending September.
Dealers said supplies had remained thin as the 1996/97 season headed towards its end.
The bulk of the current season's cotton crop, estimated at 17 million 170-kg bales, had been marketed.
"There is not much cotton left in the market," said Thakkar. "Widespread rains have also hampered transportation of cotton from producing centres to market places."
"There is also an acute shortage of good quality cotton," Thakkar said.
In the week to Thursday, spot Bengal-deshi rose 55 rupees to 1,060/1,120 rupees per maund (37.32 kg). Punjab F-414 gained 10 rupees to 2,070/2,090 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Kalyan cotton rose 100 to 14,200/14,700 per candy (355.56 kg) and Wagad made a similar gain to 13,000/13,200 per candy.
($1 = 40.62 Pakistani rupees)
-- Bombay Commodities +91-22-265 9000
